status: The Account owner now routes Account security read, MFA-gated family revocation and all-device revocation through the native Identity Access HTTP owner. The Account security page seed and the public Next route no longer use the retained TypeScript security command; a missing or failed native runtime is explicit and never falls back. This is a bounded owner surface cutover, not full Account owner or catalogue acceptance.
concurrentWorktreeNote: Other agents advanced the shared worktree with unrelated commits and uncommitted Finance/Learning/Inventory/Organization/Records/composition changes while this slice was being implemented. This subagent created no commit, branch, worktree or register and left those changes untouched.

scope.workflowBoundary: The qualified source slice is the signed-in Account security seed and the existing `POST /api/v1/account/security` family/all-device revocation command used by the Account security page and AccountSessions drawer. MFA enrollment/verification was already native through `/api/v1/account/iam/mfa/{enroll,verify}` and is unchanged. Central login/directory linking, profile/language/theme, role/Company/account switching, authorized package areas, emergency-access administration, invitation/recovery administration, Directory administration and browser acceptance remain outside this slice.
scope.nativeOwnerReused: The existing `erpx_server_identity_access::public::account_security` domain/application/PostgreSQL/HTTP implementation and the existing private-development router mount. No new Rust business logic, SQL, migration or composition mount was added.
scope.transport: `packages/native-sdk/src/session.ts` admits only the exact `/api/v1/account/security` path to the native Account ingress and forwards one bounded `Idempotency-Key` header for POST. The Next Account security route now always delegates to `nativeAccountHttp`; a missing/invalid native configuration or upstream failure is an explicit 503/error response and never re-enters the retired TypeScript handler.
scope.ssr: `currentAccountSecurity` now reads the signed-in security seed through the validated private native Account transport using the current request Host/Cookie. It no longer calls `accountSessionSecurity` or opens a Control transaction for the seed. Emergency-access display remains the existing retained Identity read because that workflow is not part of this slice.
scope.securityPropertiesPreserved: Native policy ownership, Account-audience host/origin checks, current-session and fresh-MFA checks, opaque account/family handles, expected revision/CAS, exact idempotency receipt replay, session-family and all-device revocation, Holding child invalidation, receipt/audit persistence, rollback and post-command source readback remain in the existing native owner implementation and its tests.
